In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recoil velocity of a binary system of nonspinning black holes in quasiequilibrium is ~0.1 km/s in the inspiral and plunge phases combined.
the recoil velocity of a binary system of blackholes with \nu~ 0.2 at the end of plunge is ~180 km/s.
the recoil velocity is maximum for a black hole binary system with \nu~ 0.2 and it is roughly ~180 km/s at the end of plunge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2.4PN accurate recoil velocity at the ISCO, as obtained from the inspiral phase alone, would be about ~3.5 km/s for a binary of mass ratio of 4:1.
the recoil velocity is maximum for a system with \nu~ 0.2 and the contribution from plunge to the recoil velocity is of the order 40 times the contribution from inspiral.
, the total recoil velocity of the system at the merger (end of inspiral and plunge combined) for \nu~0~0.2 is of the order 180 km/s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recoil velocity of the system at the ISCO is maximum for a symmetric binary with a mass ratio \nu~0.
the 2.3 PN accurate recoil velocity of a nonspinning binary at ISCO is about 2.3 times larger than the 2.0 PN accurate recoil velocity.
the recoil from inspiral phase is not negligible and should be included while estimating the recoil from the entire plunge phase.
